summary:
H.R. 8997, the "Energy and Water Development and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2025," appropriates funds out of any money in the Treasury not otherwise appropriated for fiscal year 2025 for the Departments of the Army (Civil Works), Interior, Energy, and related independent agencies. 

Title I appropriates funds for the Corps of Engineers–Civil, including $159,000,000 for Investigations and $3,010,000,000 for Construction, subject to work plan requirements. Section 101 establishes reprogramming thresholds and requires a baseline report within 60 days of enactment. Section 110 prohibits the Secretary of the Army from promulgating or enforcing regulations barring firearm possession at water resources development projects if the individual is not otherwise prohibited and complies with State law.

Title II appropriates funds for the Central Utah Project and the Bureau of Reclamation. Section 201 sets reprogramming limits. Sections 203 and 204 extend authorizations for the Calfed Bay-Delta Authorization Act and Reclamation States Emergency Drought Relief Act of 1991 to 2025, with increased authorization ceilings. Section 206 mandates operation of the Central Valley Project and California State Water Project per the Preferred Alternative and 2019 Biological Opinions. Section 207 amends Section 40902(a)(2) of the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (43 U.S.C. 3202(a)(2)) to broaden project eligibility. Section 209 amends the Water Infrastructure Improvements for the Nation Act and the Reclamation Wastewater and Groundwater Study and Facilities Act to extend deadlines and increase authorization ceilings.

Title III appropriates funds for Department of Energy energy programs, atomic energy defense activities, power marketing administrations, and FERC. Section 301 imposes reprogramming and notification requirements, with a waiver authority for substantial risks to health, environment, or national security. Section 309 prohibits grants or loans of $10,000,000 or greater to entities of concern as defined in Public Law 117-167. Section 315 amends Section 3 of the Natural Gas Act (15 U.S.C. 717b) to grant FERC exclusive authority over LNG facility siting and deem export/import consistent with the public interest, while preserving Presidential sanctions authority. Section 317 transfers specified unobligated balances from the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act and Public Law 117-169 to the Nuclear Energy program for Generation 3+ small modular reactor and advanced reactor demonstration projects, and amends Public Law 117-169 to adjust authorization ceilings.

Title IV appropriates funds for independent agencies, including the Nuclear Regulatory Commission. Section 402 establishes NRC reprogramming thresholds and waiver authority.

Title V contains general provisions applicable across the Act. Section 504 prohibits federal expenditure for consolidated interim storage of spent nuclear fuel absent host state, local, and tribal consent, with an exception for currently licensed facilities. Sections 505, 506, and 508 prohibit funds for Critical Race Theory, specified Executive Orders on equity and diversity, and COVID-19 mask or vaccine mandates. Section 507 prohibits discriminatory actions against persons acting on religious beliefs regarding marriage. Section 514 prohibits finalization or enforcement of specified Department of Energy energy conservation rules. Section 515 establishes a Spending Reduction Account of $0.
